title: Read, QC and plot plate reader data
text: read_bioscreen() handles Bioscreen C text export, UTF-16 comma decimals; detected converted automatically. Bioscreen C run holds one two 100-well plates, wells 1 100 plate 1 101 200 plate 2. Wells named zero-padded well within plate_id ("001" "100"), key plate_id well pair LogPhase600. position run (1 200) kept well_index. Blank column instrument writes always zero (don’t understand ). dropped default. file complete two-plate run, 567 reads 5-minute intervals 47 hours, stored xz-compressed (readers can read compressed files directly). QC steps logphase600 apply bioscreen. smoothed curve added blank correction smooth = TRUE. Wells Bioscreen plate laid square grid numbers rather lettered rows, plot_plate() draws 10 10 grid.
code: bf <- system.file("extdata", "bioscreen_full.txt.xz", package = "plateReadeR") b <- read_bioscreen(bf) b #> # A tibble: 113,400 × 6 #>    seconds  hours plate_id well  well_index    od #>      <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>    <chr>      <int> <dbl> #>  1       0 0      Plate 1  001            1 0.072 #>  2     300 0.0833 Plate 1  001            1 0.072 #>  3     600 0.167  Plate 1  001            1 0.072 #>  4     900 0.25   Plate 1  001            1 0.072 #>  5    1200 0.333  Plate 1  001            1 0.072 #>  6    1500 0.417  Plate 1  001            1 0.072 #>  7    1800 0.5    Plate 1  001            1 0.072 #>  8    2100 0.583  Plate 1  001            1 0.072 #>  9    2400 0.667  Plate 1  001            1 0.072 #> 10    2700 0.75   Plate 1  001            1 0.073 #> # ℹ 113,390 more rows b <- b |>   flag_od_range(saturation = 2) |>   blank_correct(smooth = TRUE) |>   flag_no_growth()  unique(b[c(   "plate_id",   "well",   "flag_saturated",   "flag_negative",   "flag_no_growth" )]) |>   subset(select = -well) |>   aggregate(     cbind(flag_saturated, flag_negative, flag_no_growth) ~ plate_id,     data = _,     FUN = sum   ) #>   plate_id flag_saturated flag_negative flag_no_growth #> 1  Plate 1              0             0              0 #> 2  Plate 2              0             0             30 plot_plate(b, plate = "Plate 2", smooth = TRUE)

what: Read, Format, and Quality Control Plate Reader Output
title: Read, Format, and Quality Control Plate Reader Output
text: plateReadeR reads output files (plain text, csv, Microsoft Excel) different microplate readers target audience scientists using analyze microbial growth curves. Currently implemented parsers Bioscreen C MBR, Agilent BioTek LogPhase 600 BioTek Synergy H1 Multimode Reader. parsers convert files instruments tidy data frames, runs basic quality control checks sensible defaults. user can join plate tidied results sample metadata downstream analysis. time course readers return one row per well per time point, plate_id well identifying well.

title: Read Bioscreen C output — read_bioscreen
text: path Path Bioscreen text csv file. Compressed files (.gz, .xz, .bz2, .zip) read directly. decimal_mark Decimal mark used file, "," ".". encoding File encoding. NULL (default) detected byte-order mark, falling back "UTF-16LE", Bioscreen exports use. interval_hours Nominal read interval hours (default 1/12, five minutes). Elapsed times snapped multiples snap_hours() timepoints match exactly across plates runs. Use NULL keep reported times. thin_hours Optional coarser read interval hours, example 1/3 keep one read every 20 minutes. Thinning happens times snapped interval_hours grid, keeps reads fall coarser grid, requires interval_hours set thin_hours whole multiple . NULL (default) keeps every read. wells_per_plate Number wells Bioscreen plate (100 Honeycomb plates). keep_blank TRUE, keep Blank column well "Blank" (well_index 0 plate_id NA). instrument reports column zeros, dropped default.

title: Read Bioscreen C output — read_bioscreen
text: tibble columns seconds, hours, plate_id ("Plate 1" "Plate 2", format LogPhase600 readers), well (zero-padded well within plate, "001" "100"), well_index (integer position run, 1 100 1 200) od (optical density).

title: Read Bioscreen C output — read_bioscreen
text: Bioscreen exports UTF-16LE files two preamble lines (Label Info), header line (Time, Blank, well numbers) one row readings per time point. Text exports separate fields spaces; csv exports separate commas quote value. format detected header line, read call. instrument computer often uses comma decimal mark, decimal_mark defaults ",". Bioscreen run holds either one two 100-well plates, files contain either 100 200 wells. Wells 1-100 belong plate 1 wells 101-200 plate 2. Wells named within plate zero-padded string ("001" "100"), well identified plate_id well, LogPhase600 readers. 1-200 position run kept well_index. Bioscreen report perfectly regular time intervals (example 00:30:06 versus 00:30:05), makes hard combine runs. default times therefore snapped onto regular grid snap_hours(); see interval_hours.

what: Snap elapsed time onto a regular grid — snap_hours
title: Snap elapsed time onto a regular grid — snap_hours
text: plate reader keeps clock, elapsed time meant nominal timepoint can drift second plates runs. Left , drift makes exact-value grouping (example group_by(hours) pooling replicates across plates) fracture several near-duplicate groups, shows downstream artificially jagged mean. Snapping elapsed hours onto nominal read interval grid makes timepoints line exactly.
